title: Getting started
description: Install quoin-editor, render a BlockCanvas, import its stylesheet and see what each entry adds to a page.

title: The controlled contract
description: BlockCanvas behaves like a controlled input: blocks in, onChange out, with autosave, loading, discarding and undoing a deletion in your own code.

title: Adopting existing documents
description: Move a directory of markdown files or a column of HTML into Quoin, knowing first what each conversion loses, then give the blocks ids that last, take documents back out, and check a whole corpus before you move it.

title: Theming
description: Every colour and radius comes from a --quoin- token, the stylesheet sits in one quoin cascade layer and resets nothing outside the editor.

title: Custom blocks
description: Add block types of your own with defineBlock, whose editor and preview are plain React components, and read uploads from inside them.

title: Code, image and file blocks
description: How the code, image and file blocks are typed into, selected, uploaded to and highlighted, from the mouse or the keyboard.

title: Uploads
description: Quoin stores no file itself: hand it an upload function and an asset resolver, and its image and file blocks call them.

title: Opt-in features
description: Tables, embeds and bookmarks, math, tables of contents, mentions, emoji, find and replace and document stats, each an entry of its own that a page loads only when it imports it.

title: Keyboard
description: Every key the canvas and its opt-in features answer to, as macOS and Windows or Linux write them, the same list the shortcuts dialog shows.

title: Localization
description: The seven locale packs the package ships, how a host passes one to the canvas and to each feature, and how to write a language of your own.

title: Right to left
description: How the canvas follows a page that runs right to left, what stays physical on purpose, and what is not covered yet.

title: Collaboration
description: Real-time co-editing through a Yjs document and your own provider, with an undo of your own changes and collaborators' carets and avatars.

title: Comments
description: Comment threads anchored to text, kept in your own store and reached through your callbacks, with a list beside the text or a sheet on a narrow page.

title: AI actions
description: Stream your own model's answers into the document through one callback: continue, improve, translate, summarize and more, accepted in one undo step.

title: Read-only and server rendering
description: Draw a document read-only on the canvas, in a React Server Component with QuoinView, as a diff of two versions with QuoinDiff, or as a Word file with toDocx.

title: Headless
description: The editing engine and its editable view without the canvas UI, for a host that draws its own chrome.

title: Exports
description: What each entry of quoin-editor exports, from the canvas to the Word export.

title: Engine reference
description: Every export of quoin-editor/engine with its signature: the document, steps, commands, markdown and the editor.

title: Headless reference
description: Every export quoin-editor/headless adds to the engine: the hook, the editable view, the controller and the DOM map.

title: Accessibility
description: What Quoin's test suites check for keyboard, screen reader and colour access, and what is not checked yet.

title: FAQ
description: Why the package is called quoin-editor, what the name means, what a paste from a word processor keeps, which frameworks it supports and what its semantic versioning promises.

title: The history of the stylesheet
description: Why Quoin's tokens carry a --quoin- prefix and its rules sit in one quoin cascade layer, both since 0.2.0, and what a host upgrading from 0.1 has to do.
